sources.ref: Topping Home web app v1.17.0 (https://home.toppingaudio.com/): the EQ editor's limits and filter types, how it starts a session, reads the stored configs and writes one, and how it creates, renames and deletes one

meta.notes: What Topping's web app does with its DACs on USB id 0x152a:0x8750; checked on a DX5 II only (see its profile). The ranges are the app's editor limits, not verified firmware limits: 10 bands, 20 to 20000 Hz in whole Hz, gain -12 to +12 dB in steps of 0.1, Q 0.1 to 15 in steps of 0.0001, a pre-gain of -12 to +12 dB in steps of 0.1, and peak, low and high shelf, low-pass and high-pass filters (the app hides the gain of the last two). The device is told the frequency in Hz, the gain in tenths of a dB and Q in ten-thousandths. A config holds 11 bands per channel; the app shows 10 and writes the 11th switched off. A config holds each channel apart, and the app's editor edits left and right alike or apart. The DX5 II was seen to keep them apart, so its profile says the channels are independent and the handler writes and reads them apart there; on the other four the handler writes both the same and reads the left channel. The app takes the pre-gain's wire value from a table, and computes it instead for the D900; the handler does the same, because the app reads a value that is not in its table as the neighbouring 0.1 dB step and writes that back when it connects (seen with a DX5 II). The table is one 0.1 dB step off above +7.7 dB and below -10.3 dB and wrong at +3.5 and -4.9 dB, so there the device applies a slightly different gain than the number says, as it does from Topping's app. The table repeats the step before at -4.9, -10.4 and +7.8 dB; for those the handler sends a value halfway to the next step, which the app reads as the step meant. The app sends no save command after a config's parameters, so whether a write survives a power cycle is unknown. The presets are the device's stored configs: a list the user names (up to 15 ASCII characters) and can have fewer of than listed, so the presets listed here are the room a device has, and the names are its own. The app adds a config after the last one, renames one and deletes one, after which the later ones move down. The bridge does the same on the DX5 II and DX9 Discrete, except that its new config is empty where the app's is a copy of the active one; it writes only a config that exists. Elsewhere the app allows Q up to 20, and its text import clamps to 20; the editor's 15 is used. The app keeps a session alive with a heartbeat every 1 or 5 s, which the bridge does not send. devicePEQ has no Topping support (it turned Topping detection off).
